newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA FUEL OIL - FIRM ON TIGHT SUPPLIES, NEW DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: ASIA FUEL OIL - FIRM ON TIGHT SUPPLIES, NEW DEMAND.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market firmed on Tuesday as buyers emerged at higher levels on tight prompt supplies, traders said.
Trading broke clear of the previous range of between $102.00 and $103.00 per tonne after a 20,000-tonne cargo traded at $103.50 on a free-on-board Singapore basis, up $1.00 from last trade on Friday.
A Singapore trader bought the September 7-11 lifting cargo from a European major. Another buyer was seen for a end August cargo at $102.50 per tonne.
"Fuel oil is up almost a dollar from yesterday...I think people have realised that the market is quiet tight," one trader said.
In the swaps market, September fuel oil was last quoted at $103.25/$104.00 per tonne, up from Monday's $102.50/$103.50, brokers said. It traded earlier in the day at $103.00 and 103.25, they said.
Traders said the firmer prices was partly due to expectations that a major who was offering cargoes over the past week might cease offering after managing to sell several cargoes.
Also the upbeat market was attributed to talks that China is gearing up to buy spot cargoes for delivery in late September or October.
Traders said Chinese traders have already began buying September paper over the past few days.
The squeeze on prompt barrels was also seen in the bunker market where ship owners are paying up to $5.00 per tonne more for cargoes for delivery over the next few days.
Bunkers for delivery 7-10 days out was quoted at $104-106 per tonne for 380-cst and at $107-109 for 180-cst.

Traders said the three-day closure of South Korean ports over the weekend to Monday due to Typhoon Tina has lead to a berth congestion with some tankers having to wait for up to one-week before it can discharge cargoes.
